analysis.title: The Big Picture, Fourth Quarter 2026
key_insights: Western Asset is selectively constructive on fixed income. Resilient growth and energy-related inflation favor a selective approach, and it expects further US monetary tightening.

US growth is above trend in 2H26, supported by AI investment, consumers and corporate earnings. A prolonged US-Iran war raises energy inflation risk, while wage pressure is subdued. Recession risk is low.
The firm expects 10-year US yields to stabilize in a 4.75%-5.50% range. Geopolitical risk and tighter financial conditions may push credit spreads wider.

Europe's data keeps surprising to the upside, and the ECB keeps a hawkish bias to head off second-round inflation effects. The positioning is a modest overweight in duration with a curve-steepening bias.

UK activity has beaten market and BoE forecasts. The labor market is softening gradually and pay growth is above target. The firm favors a small overweight in 5-year real-yield duration. The October budget is a credibility test for the new Chancellor.

Canada: the BoC is expected to hold rates well into 2027. The RBA resumed tightening, and unemployment is rising in Australia. The BoJ is expected to hike at a faster pace, though the firm thinks the market has already priced the hikes and will begin pricing the end of the cycle.
China is largely insulated from energy costs and inflation is not a concern. The firm expects Chinese government bond yields to grind lower and the yuan to stay stable.

Mexico: Banxico is on hold but fed tightening and narrowing rate differentials are driving peso volatility. India: more than 2.5 hikes are priced by year-end and Bloomberg Global Aggregate inclusion is the next catalyst for local bonds. Brazil: Lula's reelection brings policy continuity, but the firm expects gradual fiscal deterioration and stays cautious.

US IG credit fundamentals are strong, but spreads repriced wider on heavy AI-related issuance. The firm is overweight money center banks and prefers supply-driven underperformers such as hyperscalers over outperformers such as chemicals and refiners.

European IG spreads look more attractive after repricing, but dispersion is rising. Preference is for financials, utilities and select property companies. In Australia, record AUD supply (the largest-ever AUD corporate bond, from Alphabet) left an overhang, and issuance is expected to slow into year-end.

US HY offers all-in yields above 8% with spreads just over 300 bps, and the firm expects further tightening. European HY spreads are around 350 bps, the widest YTD. The firm focuses on BB/B issuers because CCC issues have underperformed.
Bank loans: recent weakness is seen as a buying opportunity in BB and B+/B loans, with caution on B- loans after greater spread widening.

CLOs: AAA and BBB tranches are favored. AAA spreads near 125 bps yield about 5.25% now and 6.0% forward. BBB spreads near 300 bps yield about 7.0% now and 7.75% forward. The firm selectively targets BBs.

Agency MBS spreads have narrowed but stay attractive versus Treasuries and high-quality corporates. Refinancing is limited with mortgage rates at 7%. The firm favors higher coupons in 30-year MBS, lower coupons in 20-year MBS and out-of-index allocations.

Non-agency RMBS: neutral on home prices, with rising supply and weak affordability. CMBS: 2026 is on pace for the highest new-issue volume since 2007. The firm is overweight Mezzanine and BIG SASB but cautious on short-term refinancing risk.
ABS: the firm favors moving up the capital structure and is constructive on higher-end consumer, fiber broadband and aircraft lease ABS. Low-income consumers are more exposed to higher rates.

Long-dated TIPS real yields are historically high, but the firm does not expect TIPS to outperform nominals while the Fed is fighting inflation. Front-end TIPS find support if oil spikes. Japan's 10-year breakeven at 2.2% looks fair.
Long-dated, high-quality taxable munis are fair value to slightly attractive. The firm expects spreads to stay within plus or minus 10 bps on tight supply and strong institutional demand.

EM debt: the firm favors high-yield sovereigns with improving fundamentals and IMF support, and high-real-yield local markets with adequate carry, mainly in Latin America and South Africa. It is defensive on Asian FX, especially energy importers. It expects a resilient USD and FX volatility.

EM corporates: fundamentals are sound, spreads are tight and energy and refined-product costs will differentiate issuers. The firm prefers issuer selection and new-issue participation over broad beta.

Industry views: overweight the strongest European and US banks, with 10-year senior bank debt still trading wide of the IG index. Market weight global autos. Energy could face oversupply once the conflict resolves.

Consumer-facing sectors face margin pressure. Food and beverage spreads widened on deteriorating credit fundamentals the firm expects to persist. Retail faces elevated holiday promotions and online competition. Managed care is starting to inflect while providers are negative.

Technology: AI infrastructure demand is strong, but persistent debt supply is increasing credit dispersion. Software is split between AI disruption fears and monetization, and AI ROI is unproven in IT services.

Utilities are free-cash-flow negative, rely on debt and hybrid issuance, and are operating closer to downgrade thresholds. European utilities have held up, with most issuers maintaining or raising FY26 guidance. The firm is overweight European telcos with low M&A risk and stable toplines.
Pharma: underweight IG and market weight HY. The firm expects more IG M&A into year-end and focuses in HY on names with visible credit catalysts such as rising stars, LMEs and M&A.

sector_views.sector: US money center banks and strongest European banks
sector_views.rationale: De-risked business models, robust balance sheets and stringent regulation. 10-year senior bank debt still trades wide of the IG index.
Stable topline, lower costs, low macro correlation and low M&A risk for telcos. Utilities have resilient earnings and cash flow.
Market weight. US demand should moderate after last year's pre-buy and EV tax credit changes, and valuations are tight.
Stressed consumer and lack of pricing power. Spreads widened on credit deterioration the firm expects to persist.
Underweight IG pharma and market weight HY, with more IG M&A expected into year-end.
AI demand supports infrastructure buildout, but debt supply is increasing credit dispersion and software is split on AI disruption.
Free-cash-flow negative from growing capital budgets, with debt reliance and management teams operating closer to downgrade thresholds.

earnings_insights: Western Asset is watching Q3 earnings for signs of elevated consumer spending despite rising gas prices, rising interest rates and low savings rates.
The firm expects strong Q3 earnings and positive forward guidance to support further US HY spread tightening.
Managed care earnings are starting to inflect, with 2026 a transition year and growth expected in 2027 and 2028. Providers are expected to stay negative in 3Q26 earnings.
Most European utility issuers have maintained or upgraded FY26 guidance.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight money center banks within US IG corporate credit
trade_ideas.rationale: Strongest banks have de-risked business models and robust balance sheets.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight AAA and BBB rated CLO tranches
trade_ideas.rationale: AAA spreads near 125 bps yield about 5.25% now and BBB spreads near 300 bps yield about 7.0%.

trade_ideas.description: Small overweight duration in UK 5-year real yields
trade_ideas.rationale: UK inflation risks remain but the firm favors a small overweight in 5-year real yields.

trade_ideas.description: Favor higher coupons in 30-year agency MBS and lower coupons in 20-year MBS
trade_ideas.rationale: Spreads remain attractive versus Treasuries with limited refinancing at 7% mortgage rates.

trade_ideas.description: Buy weakness in BB and B+/B bank loans
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong fundamentals largely offset higher borrowing costs and recent spread widening is seen as an opportunity.
trade_ideas.risk: Greater spread widening in B- loans warrants caution.

risk_factors: Prolonged US-Iran war driving energy inflation higher.
Geopolitical risk and tighter financial conditions pushing credit spreads wider.
Heavy US IG issuance tied to AI capex, up 30% year over year.
Housing affordability and refinancing risks in mortgage and CMBS sectors.
Low-income consumer exposure to higher rates and deteriorating real wage growth.
EM divergence in fiscal, inflation and currency risks, plus El Nino monsoon risk in India and EM inflation.
Brazil fiscal deterioration under the new Lula government.
Utilities operating closer to downgrade thresholds as capex and debt rise.
Unproven AI ROI and persistent debt supply raising credit dispersion in technology.
vol_and_positioning: Rate volatility has reduced yield-buyer activity in Australian dollar credit.
The firm expects FX volatility and a resilient USD, favoring high real yields and adequate carry in EM local markets.
Credit dispersion is increasing in US and European IG as valuations and issuer prospects diverge.
geopolitical: A prolonged US-Iran war raises energy inflation risks and supports the Fed tightening call.
US-China relations are in a managed detente, which supports China's external strength.
Energy supply disruption and inventory drawdowns tied to the conflict drive energy industry performance, with oversupply possible once it resolves.
Geopolitical issues have raised freight rates and raw material costs for retailers and transportation.
Canadian businesses face uncertain US trade policy, and a bilateral US-Mexico trade agreement could reduce uncertainty for Mexico.

tension_points.bull_case: US IG fundamentals are strong and US HY, at just over 300 bps OAS, should tighten further on strong technicals, fundamentals, Q3 earnings and positive guidance.
tension_points.bear_case: Geopolitical risk and tighter financial conditions may push credit spreads wider. US IG spreads are tight against heavy AI-related issuance, and consumers face rising gas prices, rising rates and low savings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q3 earnings failing to show elevated consumer spending despite rising gas prices, interest rates and low savings rates.

theme_stances.key_argument: Resilient US growth and energy-related inflation reinforce the expectation of further Fed tightening.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect further Fed tightening with 10-year yields stabilizing at 4.75%–5.50%

CLO relative value remains compelling in a higher-for-longer rate environment.
